classification.difficultyReason: Introduce symbolic base angles for both isosceles triangles and combine their triangle sums with the reflex angle's complement around B to prove a general doubling relationship.

content.prompt: Each of $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle CBD$ in the figure below is isosceles. Prove that the measure of reflex $\angle ABD$ is twice the measure of $\angle ACD$.

spec.description: Two joined isosceles triangles with one tick on AB, BC and BD; a red reflex sector at B and a blue full ACD sector at C.
spec.mathematics: AB=BC=BD. The marked angle at B is reflex ABD; the marked angle at C includes both ACB and BCD.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and requested angle regions are visible.

answer.short:
Reflex $\angle ABD=2\angle ACD$.

Use equal base angles in both isosceles triangles, then subtract the two angles at $B$ from $360^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Let $\angle BAC=\angle BCA=x$ and $\angle BCD=\angle BDC=y$, since the triangles are isosceles. By the angle sum of a triangle,
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABC&=180^\circ-2x\\\angle CBD&=180^\circ-2y\\\angle ACD&=x+y.\end{align*}$$
Angles at a point sum to $360^\circ$, so
$$\begin{align*}\text{reflex }\angle ABD&=360^\circ-(180^\circ-2x)-(180^\circ-2y)\\\text{reflex }\angle ABD&=2x+2y\\\text{reflex }\angle ABD&=2(x+y)\\\text{reflex }\angle ABD&=2\angle ACD.\end{align*}$$
